disease_label_per_paper: Anti-GABAB receptor antibody autoimmune encephalitis associated with clear cell renal cell carcinoma
presentation_summary: 58-year-old man presented to the emergency department with two days of stomachache and unconsciousness.
Non-contrast brain CT showed no obvious abnormality.
Abdominal CT showed a 3.9 x 3.8 cm contrast-enhancing right renal mass.
ECG showed sinus tachycardia at 123 bpm; routine blood test showed WBC 25.34 x 10^9/L with neutrophils 83.6%.
During treatment he had another generalized seizure with oxygen saturation falling to 83%, requiring emergency tracheal intubation.
CSF showed normal opening pressure 110 mmH2O, 7 leukocytes, protein 520 mg/L, glucose 4.88 mmol/L, and chloride 125.7 mmol/L.
Viral serologic and CSF tests for rubella, CMV, HSV, and EBV were negative.
EEG showed abnormal slow and sharp-wave rhythms in right frontal and frontal mid-temporal regions with intermittent generalized slow waves and higher amplitude in the left frontal area.
CSF paraneoplastic antibody testing showed only anti-GABAB receptor antibodies positive.
Symptoms did not improve after two weeks of nutritional neurologic and immunomodulatory treatment; laparoscopic radical nephrectomy found clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
After nephrectomy plus immunotherapy, seizures stopped on levetiracetam and he improved to independent living with mild cognitive impairment at 12 months.
